pr_comments:
Looks like this was updated as part of https://github.com/rumpl/moby/pull/45

Which upstreamed changes from;

- https://github.com/rumpl/moby/pull/45

cc @rumpl @ndeloof PTAL (you may have more context around this)

> Also I'm concerned about the rwlayer.Unmount() which is not done now on errors, but I really
> don't know the implications.

Unmount should be called regardless of error after the mount has succeeded. Not unmounting won't prevent the layer release from failing as that will always attempt to unmount. In this case, an exported filesystem may remain mounted longer than intended after an export, such as after a container exits.

> Unmount should be called regardless of error after the mount has succeeded. Not unmounting won't prevent the layer release from failing as that will always attempt to unmount. In this case, an exported filesystem may remain mounted longer than intended after an export, such as after a container exits.

Not sure if I understood correctly. This means that when releasing the layer it will try to unmount it? So, calling unmount is not required?

> This means that when releasing the layer it will try to unmount it? So, calling unmount is not required?

No, releasing the layer will not always unmount it. The unmount will be forced when the layer is removed, but that is only after the last release. The layer could still be in use elsewhere, that is why it is good to call unmount for every mount, especially in a case like this where the filesystem is no longer in use.

See https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/layer/layer.go#L119
```
	// Unmount unmounts the RWLayer. This should be called
	// for every mount. If there are multiple mount calls
	// this operation will only decrement the internal mount counter.
```

Each call to Unmount will end up calling the graphdriver's Put method, such 
as https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/daemon/graphdriver/overlay2/overlay.go#L623

When the last reference is released, it will eventually call the graphdriver's Remove method, which will ensure everything is unmounted, such as https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/daemon/graphdriver/overlay2/overlay.go#L494 . However, you cannot know that you are the last one to release and if you don't Unmount, you may be leaking a mount until that happens.
@dmcgowan Thank you for the clarification. Really helpful :blush:

Also, please remove the `fixes #48516` prefix from the commit title - it produces unnecessary Github linkings 😄 
Thanks!

### Reproduce

~~~bash
# Initilize a clean docker fs
systemctl stop docker
rm -r /var/lib/docker
systemctl start docker

# Check overlay2 size
du -shx /var/lib/docker/overlay2
ls -la /var/lib/docker/overlay2

# Pull random image
docker pull redis:7.4.0

# Check overlay2 size
du -shx /var/lib/docker/overlay2
ls -la /var/lib/docker/overlay2

# Create a container and export it
docker create --name test redis:7.4.0
docker export test --output="/tmp/test.tar"

# Remove the container and the image
docker rm test
docker rmi redis:7.4.0

# Check overlay2 size
du -shx /var/lib/docker/overlay2
ls -la /var/lib/docker/overlay2
~~~

### Expected behavior

Executing `docker rmi` / `docker system prune` after running `docker create` + `docker export` + `docker rm` should delete unused/dangling layers.

review_comments:
Also trying to look what error this is checking for;

- ❌ _not_ the error produced at line 24 is unrelated (return early)
- ✅ the error produced  line 35 (`rwlayer.Mount`) is the one handled here (i.e., it the mount failed, we will try to release the layer)
- ❓ but errors returned by `fn(basefs)` are not considered.

So, if the intent was to release when the mount failed, this wouldn't have to be a defer, and could be put in the error-handling block here; https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/5098132d84d3c20afd05453e430b5029e770fcc1/daemon/images/image_exporter.go#L37-L40

But indeed, if releasing only happens on an error, then there should likely be other code handling the release (which may be outside of this function, or as part of the `fn(basefs)`.

If it's the caller's responsibility (or the `fn`'s responsibility) to release the layer, that should at least be documented 😅

`PerformWithBaseFS` looks to be used in 1 location, and AFAICS that doesn't release the layer; https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/5098132d84d3c20afd05453e430b5029e770fcc1/daemon/export.go#L45-L58
